messages.subject: significance threshold for interactions
messages.body_plain:
Hi.
I'm an extreme novice at R/qtl (i.e. i started last week). I'm mostly
interested in finding epistasis between nonadditive QTLs (admittedly
in response to reviewer requests!). Luckily, I've gotten to the point
where I create the heat map and generate the (in my case) 4 page long
list of lod scores.

My question is... how do you determine the significance threshold for
a particular trait?

I thought I'd put the question out there before I screw everything up.
Thus far, I've run permutations with scantwo, but like it says in the
manual, that takes a LONG time (i have 28 traits...)! i've also added
the "hot" interactions to my formula for the fitqtl command. None of
my "hot spots" were significant when compared to the significance
threshold given by scantwo, but 3 were significant in the ANOVA table.
What have I done?!
Thank you very much!

[background: i'm working with a backcross mapping populations between
two plant species and ~80% of the markers were genotyped]

messages.body_plain:
See our discussion of the interpretation of scantwo results at the
following:

   http://www.rqtl.org/tutorials/new_summary_scantwo.pdf

I would start with 100 permutations for a single trait, to get a sense
of the numbers.

karl

messages.subject: Variance explained by QTL
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I have a backcross mapping population of apple trees. Phenotype data
is available on all 325 projeny, but genotyping (not selectively) done
on a random subset of 115 - 125 for 5 different markers of a Linkage
group. All marker data are nearly on the same set of individuals. I
have done an analysis using R/qtl and found a putative QTL on the
Linkage group. I would like to estimate the variance explained by this
QTL. I made a qtl object for this position and used fitqtl(....,
formula=y~Q1). Do I need to adjust the sample size for the missing
genotype data, i.e. 'n' in the formula 100*(1-10^(-2*LOD/n))?

This is what the summary() gives:

       df        SS        MS      LOD     %var Pvalue(Chi2)  Pvalue
(F)
Model   1  53.66034 53.660345 5.388705 7.329723 6.307492e-07
6.9611e-07
Error 324 678.43203
2.093926
Total 325
732.09238

The QTL position is on a marker which has 115 non-missing genotypes.
If I use n = 115 instead and the above formula, the estimated
%variation is 19.4% Cf. 7.3.

The second question: I see only the "result.full" and "lod" fields,
not the "est". Is this because of the single qtl model? How do I get
the QTL effect and its SE?

Thank you very much in advance.

messages.body_plain:
On Feb 10, 2009, at 8:59 PM, Nihal wrote:

> I have a backcross mapping population of apple trees. Phenotype data
> is available on all 325 projeny, but genotyping (not selectively) done
> on a random subset of 115 - 125 for 5 different markers of a Linkage
> group. All marker data are nearly on the same set of individuals. I
> have done an analysis using R/qtl and found a putative QTL on the
> Linkage group. I would like to estimate the variance explained by this
> QTL. I made a qtl object for this position and used fitqtl(....,
> formula=y~Q1). Do I need to adjust the sample size for the missing
> genotype data, i.e. 'n' in the formula 100*(1-10^(-2*LOD/n))?
>
> This is what the summary() gives:
>
>       df        SS        MS      LOD     %var Pvalue(Chi2)  Pvalue
> (F)
> Model   1  53.66034 53.660345 5.388705 7.329723 6.307492e-07
> 6.9611e-07
> Error 324 678.43203
> 2.093926
> Total 325
> 732.09238
>
> The QTL position is on a marker which has 115 non-missing genotypes.
> If I use n = 115 instead and the above formula, the estimated
> %variation is 19.4% Cf. 7.3.

In theory it would be fine to use the full set of individuals, but with
the multiple imputation approach you would need to do *many* imputations
with so much missing genotype data.

And so I would recommend omitting the ungenotyped individuals and
focusing
on the results with just the genotyped individuals.

> The second question: I see only the "result.full" and "lod" fields,
> not the "est". Is this because of the single qtl model? How do I get
> the QTL effect and its SE?

You need to call fitqtl with the argument get.ests=TRUE

karl

messages.subject: Covariate in multiple columns
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to make a covariate object by pulling genotype data from
multiple markers (or markers from single chromosome). Assigning a
single marker as covariate worked nicely. So I tried

> cov <- pull.geno(cross, chr=1)
> cov <- cross$geno[[1]]$data[,1:7]

but both gave this warning below and scanone generated nonspecific LOD
scores (all > 100).

1: In checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar,
perm.strata,  ... :
  addcovar appears to be over-specified; consider dropping columns.

I know that pull.pheno(cross, c("sex", "age")) works beautifully,
which will generate 2 column object. So I manually made 2 column
object with random number and used it as covariate but still no luck.

Thanks!
Murim

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Covariate in multiple columns
messages.body_plain:
The problem is likely collinearity of the covariates in the linear
model that you are fitting.  That is, the model is over-determined.
Consider the examples below.

I would suggest using only one or a few of the markers on the
chromosome as additive covariates.

karl
------

 > data(fake.bc)
 > fake.bc <- fill.geno(fake.bc)
 > fake.bc <- calc.genoprob(fake.bc, step=1)
 > out <- scanone(fake.bc)

 > cov <- pull.geno(fake.bc, chr=1)
 > out.a1 <- scanone(fake.bc, addcovar=cov)
 > plot(out.a1)

   [no problems]

 > cov <- pull.geno(fake.bc, chr=c(1,2,5))
 > out.a2 <- scanone(fake.bc, addcovar=cov)
 > plot(out.a2)

   [no problems]

 > cov <- pull.geno(fake.bc, chr=c(5,13))
 > out.a3 <- scanone(fake.bc, addcovar=cov)
There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
 > warnings()
Warning messages:

1: In checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar,
perm.strata,  ... :
   addcovar appears to be over-specified; consider dropping columns.

2: X'X matrix is singular.
...

 > plot(out.a3)

   [LOD scores all > 300]

messages.subject: QTL effects in a two-part model
messages.subject_clean: QTL effects in a two-part model
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I have another pseudo BC population of apple trees. The phenotype is
the proportion of total infected length on 10 shoots / seedling
(shoots were artificially inoculated). The two-part model seems the
most appropriate. Of the 136 seedling trees 28 are 0, 13 NA and 95 are
>0. I fitted a two-part model. There is evidence of a large QTL. Is
there a way getting QTL effects for the two components, p and mu? I
guess the fitqtl() uses only the "normal" model? Escapes (false
negatives) can occur in this type of data.

Thanks very much

Nihal

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL effects in a two-part model
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] QTL effects in a two-part model
messages.body_plain:
We don't currently have a way to pull out the estimated parameters in
the two-part model.  The estimates are calculated within the C code
that does the genome scan, but they are not returned to R.

karl
